title: Escaped line-break text inside a credential value
description: The text of a credential value contains an escaped line break (backslash and n) in a serialization such as a JSON string, or as plain characters in a log line with no decoder involved.
semantics: Decoding a JSON string turns the escape into a real line feed, which sits inside the decoded value: that inserts a separator, it does not rebuild the credential. In text no decoder reads, the two characters are literal. Policy (maintainer-only, ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 3): the fragments are protected whatever a consumer does with the escape; the reconstruction facts stay as stated.

applicability.rationale: Carrier-level: independent of the credential family.

evidenceBasis.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 3 (#95)): the fragments of a value interrupted by escaped line-break text are protected and the outcome is must-flag. RFC 8259 states which characters must be escaped in a JSON string; nothing cited says a reader removes the escape, so the reconstruction stays unresolved as a fact and the outcome rests on the policy. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: Control characters U+0000 through U+001F must be escaped in a JSON string, and the escape n denotes the line feed U+000A.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Maintainer-only (ADR 0020): decided by the sole maintainer, not reviewed, not independent validation; queued for retro-review (#154).
